chapterTitle: Heat Capacity and Modes of Heat Transfer
keyPoints: Heat required per unit mass per kelvin
modelAnswer: Specific heat capacity is the heat required to raise the temperature of unit mass of a substance by 1 K. It is calculated using c = Q/(mΔT), where Q is heat energy, m is mass, and ΔT is the temperature change. Its SI unit is J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹.
stem: What is meant by specific heat capacity of a substance? Write its formula and SI unit.

chapterTitle: Heat Capacity and Modes of Heat Transfer
keyPoints: Conduction transfers heat by particle collisions in solids
Kinetic theory: particles transfer energy to neighbours
Free electrons make metals good conductors
modelAnswer: Conduction is heat transfer through direct contact in which particles transfer energy by collisions without bulk movement. In solids, kinetic theory explains that heated particles vibrate more and pass energy to neighbouring particles. Metals conduct well because free electrons move rapidly through the metal and transfer heat efficiently.
stem: What is conduction? Explain it on the basis of kinetic theory of solids. What makes metals better conductors than other substances?

chapterTitle: Heat Capacity and Modes of Heat Transfer
keyPoints: Day: sea breeze from sea to land
Night: land breeze from land to sea
modelAnswer: During the day, land heats faster than the sea because land has lower specific heat. Air above the land warms, expands, becomes less dense and rises, so cooler air from the sea moves inland: this is a sea breeze. At night, land cools faster while the sea stays warmer; air above the sea rises and cooler air from land moves seaward: this is a land breeze.
stem: How do land and sea breezes form, and what role does temperature difference between land and sea water play in these breezes?
